project.name: hearthmail
project.description: Hearthmail is a cross-platform Flutter email client (macOS first) for any IMAP/SMTP account, with a private AI assistant — smart inbox sorting, summaries, reply drafting, natural-language and semantic search, translation — that runs entirely on local models through Ollama.

nodes.name: email_content.dart
nodes.summary: Defines EmailContent, a plain value object holding just the facts about one email (sender, recipients, subject, date, body, unread flag) that the AI layer needs. It is deliberately independent of the enough_mail library so the AI code can be reused and tested without a mail server.

nodes.name: EmailContent
nodes.summary: Immutable email snapshot used as the common input for every AI feature, semantic indexing and triage caching; its id is a stable key used to cache AI results. Provides a 280-char whitespace-flattened snippet and a prompt-ready rendering.

nodes.name: forPrompt
nodes.summary: Renders the email as a header block (From/To/Date/Subject) plus body for LLM prompts, truncating the body at maxBodyChars (default 12000) so a single huge email cannot overflow the model's context window.

nodes.name: triage.dart
nodes.summary: Models the AI's inbox-sorting verdict for a single email: a category (MailCategory), a priority (MailPriority), whether a human awaits a reply, and whether it looks like phishing. Includes JSON round-tripping so verdicts can be cached on disk.

nodes.name: MailCategory
nodes.summary: Enhanced enum of inbox categories (Personal, Work, Finance, Shopping, Travel, Newsletters, Promotions, Social, Updates, Other), each with a UI label and a description that is fed verbatim into the triage prompt so the model knows what each bucket means; parse() falls back to 'other' for unknown model output.

nodes.name: MailPriority
nodes.summary: Enum of high/normal/low priority with a forgiving parse() that defaults to normal when the model returns something unexpected.

nodes.name: Triage
nodes.summary: Immutable triage result (category, priority, needsReply, suspicious) with toJson/fromJson using the same snake_case keys the AI JSON schema produces, so model output can be decoded directly and cached.

nodes.name: ai_provider.dart
nodes.summary: Defines the pluggable AI backend abstraction: AiProvider (streaming chat, model listing, embeddings), the AiMessage/AiRole chat message types, AiException, and helper extensions that collect a stream into a string or decoded JSON. Exists so the app can swap Ollama for an on-device or remote model later without touching feature code.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Dart extension (AiProviderHelpers) to add complete/completeJson to every AiProvider implementation without requiring subclasses to implement them.

nodes.name: AiProvider
nodes.summary: Abstract AI backend contract: a name, listModels(), a streaming chat() that may be constrained to a JSON schema, and an optional embed() for semantic search vectors (throws by default). All AI features are written against this interface.

nodes.name: AiMessage
nodes.summary: A single chat turn (role + content) with convenience const constructors for system, user and assistant messages.

nodes.name: AiException
nodes.summary: User-facing exception type for AI failures whose message is shown directly in the UI (e.g. 'Is the Ollama app running?').

nodes.name: AiProviderHelpers
nodes.summary: Extension on AiProvider adding complete() and completeJson(), which turn the streaming chat API into one-shot string or JSON results for structured AI jobs.

nodes.name: complete
nodes.summary: Runs a chat and concatenates all streamed chunks into one trimmed string; used for short non-streamed answers such as subject suggestions.

nodes.name: completeJson
nodes.summary: Runs a schema-constrained chat at low temperature and decodes the JSON reply, falling back to extracting the outermost {...} when a model wraps JSON in prose or code fences; throws AiException if nothing parses. This is the backbone of all structured AI features (triage, search planning, ranking, event extraction).

nodes.name: ollama_provider.dart
nodes.summary: Concrete AiProvider that talks to an Ollama server over HTTP (default localhost:11434), implementing model listing, streamed chat with optional JSON-schema output, and batch embeddings. It is how Hearthmail keeps all AI fully local.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Dart's null-aware map entry ('format': ?jsonSchema) to omit the key when no schema is given, and async* generators to stream NDJSON lines.

nodes.name: OllamaProvider
nodes.summary: HTTP client for Ollama implementing AiProvider. Uses a fixed 8192-token context and 30-minute keep_alive on every call so Ollama never reloads the model between requests, and disables 'think' mode since email tasks don't benefit from long reasoning.

nodes.name: listModels
nodes.summary: GETs /api/tags with a 5-second timeout and returns sorted installed model names, translating socket errors and timeouts into friendly AiExceptions ('Is the Ollama app running?').

nodes.name: chat
nodes.summary: POSTs to /api/chat with streaming enabled and yields each content chunk from the NDJSON response as it arrives; passes the JSON schema as Ollama's 'format' for constrained output and surfaces server errors as AiExceptions.

nodes.name: embed
nodes.summary: POSTs a batch of texts to /api/embed (truncate on, 2-minute timeout) and returns one vector per input for the semantic search index.

nodes.name: _errorText
nodes.summary: Turns an Ollama error body into a helpful message, notably telling the user to 'ollama pull <model>' when a model is not installed.

nodes.name: email_ai.dart
nodes.summary: The heart of Hearthmail's private assistant: EmailAi implements every email-specific AI feature (summaries, digests, quick replies, drafting, rewriting, triage, natural-language search planning and ranking, Q&A over emails, language detection, translation and calendar-event extraction) as prompts on top of any AiProvider. Also contains EmailEvent (.ics export), RewriteStyle presets and an offline Languages guesser.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of Dart enhanced enums, collection-if inside list literals for conditional prompt lines, async* generators with yield* for streamed translation, and Dart 3 record/pattern syntax.

nodes.name: RewriteStyle
nodes.summary: Enhanced enum of draft-rework presets (Improve, Shorter, More detail, Formal, Friendly, Fix grammar, Format), each carrying a UI label and the exact instruction injected into the rewrite prompt.

nodes.name: EmailAi
nodes.summary: Facade over an AiProvider exposing all email AI features. Uses two models by design: a fast model for quick structured jobs (sorting, search, summaries, quick replies) and a writing model for anything the user will send; optional translation and embedding models; an injectable clock so date-relative prompts are testable.

nodes.name: _writerRules
nodes.summary: Builds the shared system prompt for any text the user will send: body only, natural tone, never invent facts (use [placeholders]), sign off with the user's first name, and follow the user's personal style notes.

nodes.name: summarize
nodes.summary: Streams a Markdown summary of one email (TL;DR, action items, key dates & numbers) using the fast model at low temperature.

nodes.name: digest
nodes.summary: 'Catch me up' feature: streams a Markdown briefing of many emails grouped into Needs your attention / Worth knowing / Can skip, using the writing model and today's date for deadline context.

nodes.name: quickReplies
nodes.summary: Asks the fast model (JSON-constrained) for exactly three short ready-to-send reply options and sanitizes the result to at most three non-empty strings.

nodes.name: draftReply
nodes.summary: Streams a full reply draft with the writing model, following the user's optional instruction (e.g. 'yes but Thursday') and matching the original's formality.

nodes.name: compose
nodes.summary: Streams a complete new email from rough notes plus optional recipient and subject, applying the shared writer rules.

nodes.name: rewrite
nodes.summary: Streams a reworked draft in a chosen RewriteStyle, preserving the greeting and sign-off; uses near-zero temperature for grammar-only fixes.

nodes.name: customEdit
nodes.summary: Applies a free-form edit request (e.g. 'mention the deadline is Friday') to a draft and streams the full revised email.

nodes.name: suggestSubject
nodes.summary: Generates a short subject line for a body and strips quotes and stray 'Subject:' prefixes small models tend to add.

nodes.name: triage
nodes.summary: Sorts a batch of emails in one JSON-schema-constrained call: for each [index] the model returns category, priority, needs_reply and suspicious (phishing). Category descriptions come from MailCategory so prompt and enum stay in sync; out-of-range indexes are ignored and results are keyed by EmailContent.id.

nodes.name: planSearch
nodes.summary: Converts a natural-language question into structured search filters (keywords with synonyms, from/to, subject, date range, unread/flagged/attachment flags) relative to today's date, returning a SearchPlan that can be run as an IMAP or Gmail query.

nodes.name: rankResults
nodes.summary: Re-ranks server search candidates by relevance to the query, dropping clearly irrelevant ones; returns candidate ids best-first with duplicate and range checks on the model's indexes.

nodes.name: answerFromEmails
nodes.summary: Streams a brief answer to a question ('When is my flight?') grounded only in the provided emails, citing the sender/subject and admitting when the answer isn't there.

nodes.name: detectLanguage
nodes.summary: Detects an email's language: first a fast offline Languages.guess, then a JSON-constrained model call on a 600-char sample only when unsure; returns null on short text or failure.

nodes.name: translate
nodes.summary: Streams a translation into a target language. Uses a dedicated translation model (e.g. translategemma, with its exact trained prompt and detected source language) for reading, but the writing model when forSending, since it writes more natural foreign text.

nodes.name: extractEvent
nodes.summary: Finds the single most important event/meeting/flight/deadline in an email via JSON-constrained output, resolving relative dates against today and the send date; returns an EmailEvent or null.

nodes.name: cleanDraft
nodes.summary: Static post-processor that strips code fences, 'Here is…' preambles and stray 'Subject:' lines that small models add to drafts despite instructions.

nodes.name: EmailEvent
nodes.summary: An event extracted from an email (title, start, optional end, all-day flag, location) that can be exported as an .ics file for the Calendar app.

nodes.name: toIcs
nodes.summary: Serializes the event as an RFC 5545 VCALENDAR/VEVENT string with escaped text, defaulting the end to +1 hour (timed) or +1 day (all-day).

nodes.name: Languages
nodes.summary: Static language helpers: a list of common languages for pickers, English-name to ISO code mapping (needed for translategemma prompts) and an offline language guesser.

nodes.name: guess
nodes.summary: Fast offline language guess from Unicode script ranges (Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Greek, Hebrew, Thai, …) and stop-word counts for Latin-script languages; only returns a result with a clear winner, otherwise null so the AI can decide.

nodes.name: email_html.dart
nodes.summary: Turns raw email bodies (HTML or plain text) into safe, self-contained web pages for the message viewer: strips scripts and handlers, enforces a nonce-based Content-Security-Policy, blocks remote images/tracking pixels unless allowed, embeds cid: inline images, scales wide newsletters to fit, and folds quoted reply history.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses package:html's DOM for sanitization plus a private extension on dom.Node (nextNode) to walk siblings.

nodes.name: EmailDocument
nodes.summary: Result of rendering an email for display: the final HTML plus a count of blocked remote images (so the UI can offer 'Load images'). Built only through fromHtml/fromPlain so every displayed page goes through sanitization.

nodes.name: _csp
nodes.summary: Builds the Content-Security-Policy: no scripts except the nonce'd fit script, no frames/forms/base, and images/styles/fonts only from data:/cid: unless remote content is allowed.

nodes.name: _fitScript
nodes.summary: Returns the single nonce-authorized script that zooms the body down (min 35%) when content is wider than the pane, mimicking Apple Mail for wide newsletters.

nodes.name: fromHtml
nodes.summary: Sanitizes an HTML email: removes executable/navigating elements, on* handlers and javascript: links, drops remote stylesheets, replaces remote images with a transparent pixel (removing 1x1 tracking pixels, preserving aspect ratio otherwise), inlines cid: images, folds quotes, and injects CSP/viewport/base CSS and the fit script.

nodes.name: fromPlain
nodes.summary: Wraps a plain-text email in a full HTML page with CSP, base/plain CSS and optional dark theme, using plainToHtml for the body.

nodes.name: _linkify
nodes.summary: Turns URLs, www. hosts and email addresses in an already-escaped line into clickable links (https:// or mailto:).

nodes.name: plainToHtml
nodes.summary: Converts plain text to HTML: escapes markup, renders '>' quote levels as nested blockquotes, dims the '-- ' signature, linkifies, and folds the quoted history behind '•••' when the rest of the message is mostly quotes (detecting multilingual 'On … wrote:' attributions).

nodes.name: _foldQuotes
nodes.summary: Folds quoted history in HTML replies from Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook and Yahoo into a <details> '•••' toggle, skipping nested quotes and moving Outlook's trailing header block along with the quote.

nodes.name: triage_cache.dart
nodes.summary: Per-account on-disk cache of AI triage results (a JSON file in the app support directory) so each email is sorted by the model only once, capped at 5000 entries.

nodes.name: TriageCache
nodes.summary: Map of message key to Triage backed by a JSON file per account, with an in-memory variant for tests and previews. Corrupt files are ignored (costs only a re-sort) and the oldest entries are evicted beyond 5000.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Loads (or creates) the account's triage_<id>.json cache from the application support directory, tolerating corruption.

nodes.name: putAll
nodes.summary: Adds triage results, trims to the newest 5000 entries, and rewrites the JSON file (no-op on disk for in-memory caches).

nodes.name: vector_index.dart
nodes.summary: A tiny per-account vector database for semantic email search: stores one truncated, normalized embedding per email in a custom binary file and finds matches by exact cosine similarity. Also defines EmbeddingFormat, which phrases queries and documents with each embedding model's preferred task prefixes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Float32List and ByteData for a compact little-endian binary format ('LMVI' magic, version 1) and Dart 3 records for (IndexedMail, score) results.

nodes.name: IndexedMail
nodes.summary: Location of an indexed email on the server (key, folder path, UID, date) so a search hit can be re-fetched over IMAP.

nodes.name: VectorIndex
nodes.summary: In-memory list of embeddings with brute-force cosine search, persisted per account. Design choice: at ~20k emails x 512 dims (~40 MB) a full scan takes ~10 ms, beating approximate indexes like HNSW on accuracy and simplicity. Vectors are cut to 512 dims (Matryoshka-style models) and normalized; oldest mail is evicted beyond 20,000 entries.

nodes.name: oldestIn
nodes.summary: Returns the oldest indexed date for a folder, used to know where background indexing should continue.

nodes.name: _prepare
nodes.summary: Truncates a vector to 512 dimensions and L2-normalizes it so a dot product equals cosine similarity.

nodes.name: add
nodes.summary: Inserts or replaces an email's prepared vector and marks the index dirty for saving.

nodes.name: remove
nodes.summary: Removes an entry in O(1) by swapping the last entry into its slot and updating the position map.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Scores every stored vector against the prepared query by dot product, keeps those above minScore and returns the top `limit` (IndexedMail, score) pairs best first.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Evicts the oldest entries beyond maxEntries, serializes the index to the LMVI binary format and writes it atomically via a temp file and rename.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Loads an account's vectors_<id>.bin, validating magic, version and model name (vectors from a different model are not comparable, so it starts fresh); a damaged file just triggers re-indexing.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Cancels pending saves, clears memory and deletes the index file (used when removing an account or rebuilding).

nodes.name: EmbeddingFormat
nodes.summary: Phrases search queries and email documents in the format each embedding model family (embeddinggemma, qwen3-embedding, nomic) was trained on, which noticeably improves search quality.

nodes.name: query
nodes.summary: Wraps a search query with the model family's query prefix (e.g. 'task: search result | query: …').

nodes.name: document
nodes.summary: Formats an EmailContent as an embedding document (subject, sender, date, first 1500 chars of body) with the model family's document prefix.

nodes.name: app_state.dart
nodes.summary: The app's central state and controller: a single ChangeNotifier (AppState) that owns all connected accounts, the current mailbox view, message actions, sending (undo-send, scheduled send, follow-ups), snoozes, block/mute rules, unsubscribe, attachments, AI setup and inbox sorting, semantic indexing, and keyword/AI search. Also defines the MailView, Toast, OutgoingMail and AccountSession types the UI binds to.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Expando to attach owning account and mailbox to enough_mail MimeMessage objects without wrapping them, plus Dart 3 records, patterns and null-aware collection elements (?x).

nodes.name: MailView
nodes.summary: Value type describing what the message list shows (all inboxes, a folder, priority, needs-reply, a category, search, VIP, snoozed, scheduled, follow-ups) with value equality so views can be compared and used as sidebar keys.

nodes.name: Toast
nodes.summary: A transient UI message with an optional action button (e.g. 'Undo') and duration, delivered to the UI through AppState's toast stream.

nodes.name: OutgoingMail
nodes.summary: Everything needed to send or re-open a message: sending account, recipients, subject, Markdown body, reply target, attachments, optional scheduled send time and follow-up reminder days.

nodes.name: AccountSession
nodes.summary: Runtime state of one connected account: its config, MailService connection and status, folders, paged inbox messages, triage cache, plus a vector index and a separate background IMAP connection used only for indexing.

nodes.name: AppState
nodes.summary: The single ChangeNotifier the whole UI listens to. It orchestrates accounts and IMAP connections, merged multi-account inbox views and filters, message actions, sending pipelines, local organization features (snooze, VIP, block, mute, follow-up), AI provider/model selection, background AI sorting and semantic indexing, and hybrid search; problems surface as toasts rather than exceptions.

nodes.name: refreshAi
nodes.summary: (Re)creates the OllamaProvider from settings, lists installed models (setting aiError with a hint like 'ollama pull gemma4:12b' when none), repairs saved fast/writing model choices that are no longer installed, then rebuilds EmailAi and notifies listeners.

nodes.name: embeddingModel
nodes.summary: Getter choosing the embedding model in use: empty when semantic search is off, the configured one if installed, else the best installed embedding model (preferring embeddinggemma, which tested best for email search).

nodes.name: _pickDefault
nodes.summary: Picks a default chat model by parsing the parameter size from the name (e.g. '12b') and choosing the one closest to 12B: capable enough to write well but still responsive.

nodes.name: _rebuildAi
nodes.summary: Constructs the EmailAi facade from the current provider and settings (models, user name falling back to an account display name, style notes), or null when no models are available.

nodes.name: updateSettings
nodes.summary: Persists new settings; refreshes AI when the Ollama URL changed, otherwise rebuilds EmailAi, and drops and rebuilds semantic indexes when the effective embedding model changed.

nodes.name: init
nodes.summary: App startup: opens UserData, refreshes AI, starts the 30-second housekeeping tick, connects all accounts in parallel, starts the 3-minute quiet refresh timer, then kicks off auto-sorting, a tick and background indexing.

nodes.name: _credentialsFor
nodes.summary: Loads an account's credentials from the secure store: a password, or an OAuth token wrapped with an OAuthClient that persists refreshed tokens; errors if the Google/Microsoft sign-in app isn't configured.

nodes.name: _connect
nodes.summary: Connects one account: disconnects any old session, resolves credentials, connects MailService, opens its triage cache, lists mailboxes, picks the inbox and loads the first page; failures set status=failed with a friendly error.

nodes.name: _loadInbox
nodes.summary: Fetches the first inbox page for an account, tags messages with their owner/mailbox, and runs post-fetch processing (contact learning, rules, indexing) in the background.

nodes.name: testAccount
nodes.summary: Static helper that verifies new account credentials by connecting and listing mailboxes, returning a friendly error string or null on success.

nodes.name: addAccount
nodes.summary: Stores credentials, replaces any existing session with the same id, persists the account list, connects it and starts refresh, sorting and indexing.

nodes.name: removeAccount
nodes.summary: Removes an account and all its local traces: password, connections, triage cache, vector index, and any views, selection or search results pointing at it.

nodes.name: _hiddenFromInbox
nodes.summary: Decides whether an inbox message is hidden: snoozed and not yet due, from a blocked sender, or in a muted thread.

nodes.name: openFolder
nodes.summary: Switches the list to a folder: reuses already-loaded inbox messages for an inbox, otherwise fetches the first page while guarding against the user switching folders mid-load.

nodes.name: _viewMessages
nodes.summary: Computes the message list for a MailView: merged inbox minus hidden mail, folder contents, search results, or inbox subsets filtered by AI triage (high priority or VIP, needs reply and unanswered, category), VIP or snoozed.

nodes.name: unreadFor
nodes.summary: Unread badge count for a sidebar entry, with special cases for folders, snoozed, scheduled and due follow-ups.

nodes.name: loadMore
nodes.summary: Pagination: loads the next page for the open folder (deduplicating by UID) or for every connected inbox that has more, then triggers auto-sort.

nodes.name: _loadMoreInbox
nodes.summary: Fetches the next inbox page for one account and appends unseen UIDs.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Fetches the newest inbox page for every account and prepends new mail; in quiet (timer) mode it also retries failed accounts. New mail triggers post-fetch rules, auto-sort and indexing.

nodes.name: openMessage
nodes.summary: Selects a message, downloads its full body if only headers were fetched (swapping it into all lists), then marks it read on the server.

nodes.name: _act
nodes.summary: Shared runner for message actions (read/flag/delete/archive/junk/move): performs the server action, removes the message from local lists when needed, auto-selects the next message, and reports success or errors via toasts.

nodes.name: sendMail
nodes.summary: Entry point for sending: schedules mail with a send time, otherwise delays delivery by the 'Undo send' window, showing an Undo toast that cancels the timer and reopens the draft in the composer.

nodes.name: _deliver
nodes.summary: Builds the MIME message (Markdown body, reply threading, attachments) and sends it over SMTP; on failure shows a toast with 'Open' to recover the draft.

nodes.name: _afterSent
nodes.summary: After a send, learns recipients as weighted contacts for autocomplete and records a follow-up reminder if requested.

nodes.name: _schedule
nodes.summary: Queues a message for later: copies attachments into an outbox folder so they still exist at send time, stores a ScheduledMail with threading headers in UserData, sorted by send time.

nodes.name: cancelScheduled
nodes.summary: Removes a scheduled message and deletes its copied attachments.

nodes.name: _sendScheduled
nodes.summary: Sends a due scheduled message (removing it first to avoid double sends); if sending fails it is put back to retry on the next tick.

nodes.name: saveDraft
nodes.summary: Builds the message and saves it to the account's server Drafts folder.

nodes.name: _tick
nodes.summary: Housekeeping run every 30 seconds (re-entrancy guarded): sends due scheduled mail, brings back due snoozed messages once, and clears follow-up reminders once a reply referencing the sent message arrives.

nodes.name: _bringBack
nodes.summary: When a snooze is due, ensures the message is in the inbox list (fetching it by UID if needed), marks it unread and shows a reminder toast.

nodes.name: snooze
nodes.summary: Snoozes a message until a time: stores a Snooze in UserData keyed by message, hides it from the inbox and confirms with a friendly 'I'll remind you…' toast.

nodes.name: blockSender
nodes.summary: Adds a sender to the block list and immediately re-applies rules so their existing inbox mail moves to Junk.

nodes.name: muteThread
nodes.summary: Toggles muting for a conversation (by thread key); muting immediately archives the thread's inbox messages, and future replies are archived and marked read.

nodes.name: _afterFetch
nodes.summary: Post-fetch pipeline for new mail: learns sender contacts, applies block/mute rules, then embeds the messages into the semantic index.

nodes.name: _applyRules
nodes.summary: Applies local rules to inbox messages: blocked senders go to Junk; unflagged messages in muted threads are marked read and archived.

nodes.name: markAllRead
nodes.summary: Marks every unread message in the current view as read on its server.

nodes.name: unsubscribe
nodes.summary: Leaves a mailing list using the List-Unsubscribe headers: RFC 8058 one-click POST when supported, otherwise an unsubscribe email, otherwise opening the web page; returns a human-readable outcome.

nodes.name: saveAttachment
nodes.summary: Downloads an attachment part; with open=true writes it to a temp folder and opens it in the default app, otherwise saves to Downloads with a non-clobbering 'name (n).ext' filename.

nodes.name: attachmentFiles
nodes.summary: Downloads all of a message's attachments to temporary files so they can be re-attached when forwarding.

nodes.name: addToCalendar
nodes.summary: Writes an AI-extracted EmailEvent as an .ics file (with the email subject as description) and opens it in the Calendar app.

nodes.name: indexAll
nodes.summary: Background semantic indexing of every connected account, coalescing concurrent requests (a request during a run schedules exactly one rerun).

nodes.name: _vectorsFor
nodes.summary: Lazily opens an account's VectorIndex for the current embedding model, reopening when the model changes.

nodes.name: _indexMessages
nodes.summary: Embeds not-yet-indexed messages in chunks of 16 via the provider using EmbeddingFormat.document, adds them to the account's VectorIndex and schedules a save.

nodes.name: _indexAccount
nodes.summary: Walks the account's search folder (All Mail) and Sent folder on a separate IMAP connection, fetching headers in pages of 100 and full messages only for unindexed UIDs (25 at a time), stopping after three fully-known pages or the configured depth; always saves and disconnects at the end.

nodes.name: rebuildIndex
nodes.summary: Deletes every account's vector index and re-runs indexing from scratch.

nodes.name: _semanticSearch
nodes.summary: Meaning-based search: embeds the query with the model's query prefix, searches each account's VectorIndex (min score 0.25, measured threshold for embeddinggemma), re-fetches hits by UID per folder, prunes index entries for deleted/moved mail, and returns messages best-first while remembering scores.

nodes.name: sortInboxes
nodes.summary: AI inbox sorting: collects untriaged inbox messages across accounts (optionally clearing caches with force), sorts newest-first so visible mail is sorted first, sends them to EmailAi.triage in batches of 10, caches results with progress updates, and coalesces re-sort requests.

nodes.name: _searchTargets
nodes.summary: Decides where to search: the currently open folder, or each connected account's all-mail search folder.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Hybrid search. Keyword mode runs a server-side search and appends up to 10 strongly related semantic hits. AI mode asks EmailAi.planSearch to turn the question into filters, runs them on every account (widening by dropping keywords if nothing matches), fuses with semantic matches via reciprocal rank fusion, then has the AI rank the top 30; status text is updated at each stage.

nodes.name: friendlyError
nodes.summary: Static mapper from low-level IMAP/SMTP/OAuth/network exceptions to plain-English messages (login failed, expired sign-in, no network, timeout, macOS sandbox block).

nodes.name: debugLoad
nodes.summary: Test/screenshot hook that loads fake accounts, mailboxes, messages and triage results (with an in-memory TriageCache) and an optional EmailAi without any server.

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.summary: Cancels timers and pending sends, closes streams, saves vector indexes and disconnects all IMAP connections and the AI provider.

nodes.name: features_test.dart
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the app's pure feature logic: HTML/plain email sanitization and quote folding (EmailDocument), offline language guessing, the vector index and embedding formats, MailService header helpers (unsubscribe, forged-sender detection, threading), .ics calendar export, and contact autocomplete/blocking in UserData.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Defines the flutter_test groups: EmailDocument (script/handler/remote-image blocking, inline cid images, CSP, Gmail quote folding, plain-text linkify/signature/escaping), Languages.guess, VectorIndex search/remove and EmbeddingFormat prefixes, MailService helpers, EmailEvent.toIcs and UserData contacts/blocking.

nodes.name: ai_smoke.dart
nodes.summary: Developer smoke-test script (dart run tool/ai_smoke.dart [model]) that exercises every EmailAi feature live against the local Ollama server using six realistic sample emails and a fixed clock, printing each result with timing and setting a failing exit code on errors.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Lists Ollama models, builds an EmailAi with the chosen (or first) model and a fixed date, then runs timed steps for subject suggestion, summarize, quick replies, draft reply, triage, search planning, ranking, answering, compose, formal rewrite and digest.

nodes.name: main.dart
nodes.summary: Application entry point: opens the persisted SettingsStore, builds the global AppState and mounts it via Provider, then starts connecting accounts only after the first frame so the window appears instantly. Also defines the root MaterialApp, which routes first-time users to account setup and everyone else to the inbox.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Async bootstrap: initializes Flutter bindings, opens SettingsStore, wraps AppState in a ChangeNotifierProvider and runs the app, then calls state.init() afterward so slow IMAP connections never block the first paint.

nodes.name: HearthmailApp
nodes.summary: Root stateless widget that configures light/dark Material 3 themes and picks the home screen reactively: HomePage when at least one account exists, otherwise a first-run AccountSetupPage.

nodes.name: buildTheme
nodes.summary: Static factory producing a compact Material 3 ThemeData seeded from the brand indigo for a given brightness, with flat app bars and floating snackbars; static so screenshot tooling can reuse the exact same theme.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the MaterialApp, using context.select on AppState so it only rebuilds when 'has any account' flips, and chooses HomePage vs. first-run AccountSetupPage accordingly.

nodes.name: account_config.dart
nodes.summary: Core data model for an email account's connection settings (hosts, ports, login, auth method) plus a table of known provider presets. Secrets are deliberately excluded from this model's JSON so credentials live only in the OS keychain.

nodes.name: AuthType
nodes.summary: Enum of supported sign-in methods: app password, Google OAuth or Microsoft OAuth; drives which credential path and setup UI the app uses.

nodes.name: AccountConfig
nodes.summary: Immutable description of one IMAP/SMTP account with derived helpers (effective login name, STARTTLS vs. implicit TLS by port, Gmail detection) and JSON round-tripping; the password/token is intentionally never part of it.

nodes.name: toJson
nodes.summary: Serializes the account's non-secret connection fields, including the auth type name, for storage in SharedPreferences.

nodes.name: AccountConfig.fromJson
nodes.summary: Factory that rebuilds an AccountConfig from stored JSON with defensive defaults (ports 993/465, password auth) so older saved data without newer fields still loads.

nodes.name: ProviderPreset
nodes.summary: Static catalogue of well-known providers (Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo) with server settings and app-password instructions, so most users only type their email and app password.

nodes.name: forEmail
nodes.summary: Looks up the preset whose domain list matches an email address's domain, returning null for unknown providers so the caller can fall back to autodiscovery.

nodes.name: oauth.dart
nodes.summary: Implements 'Sign in with Google / Microsoft' for IMAP/SMTP using OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and a short-lived loopback HTTP server that receives the redirect. Because the app has no backend, it uses the user's own client registration and translates provider error codes into actionable messages.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Dart 3 records for the provider server tuple and the null-aware map entry syntax ('key': ?value) to omit optional parameters.

nodes.name: OAuthClient
nodes.summary: Provider-aware OAuth client (Google or Microsoft) that knows each provider's endpoints, scopes and IMAP/SMTP servers, runs the interactive browser sign-in and refreshes tokens; HTTP client and browser opener are injectable for testing.

nodes.name: OAuthClient.google
nodes.summary: Named constructor for Google; normalizes a blank client secret to null because desktop Google apps may or may not use one.

nodes.name: OAuthClient.microsoft
nodes.summary: Named constructor for Microsoft as a public client with no secret, matching Entra 'mobile & desktop' registrations.

nodes.name: servers
nodes.summary: Getter returning the IMAP/SMTP host and port record for the provider (Gmail or Office 365) so OAuth-created accounts need no manual server entry.

nodes.name: signIn
nodes.summary: Runs the full authorization-code + PKCE flow: binds loopback servers on IPv4 (and IPv6), opens the browser to the consent page, waits up to 5 minutes for the redirect, verifies state, exchanges the code for tokens, insists on a refresh token for offline access, and reads email/name from the ID token. Always tears the servers down in a finally block.

nodes.name: refresh
nodes.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token, keeping the old refresh token when the provider does not rotate it.

nodes.name: _post
nodes.summary: POSTs a form to the token endpoint with a 30s timeout, maps network failures and non-200 responses to OAuthException with friendly text.

nodes.name: _token
nodes.summary: Converts a token-endpoint JSON response into enough_mail's OauthToken, filling defaults for expiry, scope, type and refresh token.

nodes.name: _idClaims
nodes.summary: Decodes the payload of a JWT ID token without signature verification (only used to display email/name), returning an empty map on any malformed input.

nodes.name: _describeError
nodes.summary: Translates OAuth/Entra error codes (access_denied, admin consent AADSTS codes, invalid client, org_internal) into plain-English guidance, notably for university tenants that block third-party apps.

nodes.name: _randomString
nodes.summary: Generates a cryptographically secure random string from the PKCE unreserved alphabet, used for the code verifier and CSRF state.

nodes.name: OAuthResult
nodes.summary: Value object returned by a successful sign-in: the token plus the account's email and display name.

nodes.name: OAuthException
nodes.summary: Exception carrying a user-facing message for any sign-in failure; toString returns the message so it can be shown directly in the UI.

nodes.name: settings_store.dart
nodes.summary: Persistence layer: the AppSettings model (Ollama URL, model choices, writing profile, OAuth client IDs, search and undo-send options) and SettingsStore, which keeps settings and account lists in SharedPreferences while passwords and OAuth tokens go to the OS keychain.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a private named constructor plus an async static factory (SettingsStore.open) because SharedPreferences can only be obtained asynchronously.

nodes.name: AppSettings
nodes.summary: Immutable app-wide preferences covering AI setup (Ollama URL, fast/writing/embedding/translation models), the user's writing profile, privacy toggles and OAuth registrations, with copyWith and tolerant JSON round-tripping.

nodes.name: copyWith
nodes.summary: Returns a modified copy of the settings, the standard immutable-update pattern used by every settings screen.

nodes.name: toJson
nodes.summary: Serializes all settings fields to a JSON map for SharedPreferences.

nodes.name: AppSettings.fromJson
nodes.summary: Rebuilds settings from JSON, supplying defaults for any missing key so new fields never break older saved settings.

nodes.name: SettingsStore
nodes.summary: Facade over SharedPreferences (versioned 'settings.v1' / 'accounts.v1' keys) and FlutterSecureStorage (per-account password and OAuth token entries), using the classic login keychain so unsigned local macOS builds work.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Async factory that obtains SharedPreferences and constructs the store; the only way to create one.

nodes.name: loadSettings
nodes.summary: Reads and decodes settings, falling back to defaults when absent or corrupt rather than crashing on startup.

nodes.name: saveSettings
nodes.summary: Writes the settings JSON to SharedPreferences.

nodes.name: loadAccounts
nodes.summary: Reads the stored account list and decodes each AccountConfig, returning an empty list on missing or malformed data.

nodes.name: saveAccounts
nodes.summary: Persists the list of account configs (without secrets) as JSON.

nodes.name: readPassword
nodes.summary: Reads an account's app password from the keychain.

nodes.name: writePassword
nodes.summary: Stores an account's app password in the keychain.

nodes.name: deletePassword
nodes.summary: Removes both the password and any OAuth token for an account from the keychain, used when an account is removed.

nodes.name: readToken
nodes.summary: Loads and decodes an account's stored OAuth token from the keychain, returning null if missing or unreadable.

nodes.name: writeToken
nodes.summary: Serializes and stores an account's OAuth token in the keychain.

nodes.name: account_setup_page.dart
nodes.summary: Onboarding screen for adding a mail account, offering three paths: Google OAuth, Microsoft OAuth, or an app password with provider presets and Mozilla/autoconfig discovery. It walks users through one-time OAuth app registration, tests the connection before saving, and explains provider- and university-specific failures.

nodes.name: AccountSetupPage
nodes.summary: Stateful widget entry for account setup; isFirstRun marks the initial launch when there is no account yet (no back navigation).

nodes.name: _AccountSetupPageState
nodes.summary: Holds all form controllers and flow state (chosen auth method, busy/discovering/waiting-for-browser flags, errors) and implements preset filling, server discovery, password and OAuth account creation, plus the multi-step UI.

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.summary: Disposes all text controllers to avoid leaks when the page closes.

nodes.name: _onEmailChanged
nodes.summary: On each email keystroke, matches a ProviderPreset and auto-fills IMAP/SMTP hosts and ports so known providers need no manual entry.

nodes.name: _discover
nodes.summary: For unknown domains, queries enough_mail's Discover (Mozilla ISP DB, autoconfig, DNS) once per address to fill server settings, revealing the advanced fields if nothing is found.

nodes.name: _save
nodes.summary: Validates the password form, triggers discovery if servers are missing, builds an AccountConfig, strips spaces from preset app passwords, tests the connection via AppState.testAccount, then adds the account and seeds the user's name before closing.

nodes.name: _hasClient
nodes.summary: Checks whether the user has already saved an OAuth client ID for the chosen provider.

nodes.name: _saveClient
nodes.summary: Saves the pasted Google client ID/secret or Microsoft client ID into AppSettings so the OAuth sign-in step becomes available.

nodes.name: _oauthSignIn
nodes.summary: Runs browser OAuth via the AppState-provided OAuthClient, builds an AccountConfig from the provider's server settings, verifies the mailbox connection, and stores the token; adds a hint that some universities disable IMAP for Microsoft 365.

nodes.name: _chooser
nodes.summary: Builds the three large sign-in option buttons (Google, Microsoft, app password) that set the chosen method.

nodes.name: _oauthPanel
nodes.summary: Builds the OAuth panel: either step-by-step instructions plus fields to register the user's own Google Cloud/Entra app, or the 'Continue in browser' sign-in view with progress states and an option to change the registration.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Lays out the setup page, switching between the method chooser, OAuth panel and the app-password form with preset help links, advanced server fields and the connect button.

nodes.name: settings_page.dart
nodes.summary: Settings screen for the local AI assistant (Ollama URL, fast/writing/embedding/translation models, semantic index depth), language, undo-send delay, per-account signatures, VIP and blocked senders, writing style, privacy toggles, OAuth app registrations and account management. Every change is saved immediately through AppState.

nodes.name: SettingsPage
nodes.summary: Stateful widget entry point for the settings screen.

nodes.name: _SettingsPageState
nodes.summary: Owns text controllers lazily seeded from current AppSettings and per-account signatures, and renders the settings sections, persisting each edit on change.

nodes.name: dispose
nodes.summary: Disposes the settings and signature text controllers.

nodes.name: _save
nodes.summary: Thin helper forwarding an updated AppSettings to AppState.updateSettings, giving every control a one-call save path.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds sectioned settings: AI connection status and model pickers filtered from Ollama's model list, semantic-search indexing controls, language/translation, undo send, signatures, VIP/blocked lists, writing profile, privacy, OAuth client IDs and account list with removal confirmation and 'Add account'.

nodes.name: oauth_test.dart
nodes.summary: Unit tests for OAuthClient that simulate the browser with a fake opener which follows the redirect to the real loopback server, and mock the token endpoint. They verify PKCE challenge/verifier matching, provider-specific redirect URIs, scopes and secrets, state tampering rejection, friendly error mapping and refresh-token retention.

nodes.name: _jwt
nodes.summary: Builds an unsigned fake JWT with given claims so tests can feed ID tokens to the client.

nodes.name: fakeBrowser
nodes.summary: Returns a browser-opener stub that inspects the auth URL and then fires an HTTP GET back to the app's loopback redirect (optionally with a tampered state or an error), mimicking a real provider without network access.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Defines five tests: Google sign-in end to end, Microsoft sign-in specifics, wrong-state rejection, admin-consent/access_denied messaging, and refresh keeping the old refresh token.

nodes.name: screenshots_test.dart
nodes.summary: Screenshot generator run as a Flutter widget test: renders the real app screens with fabricated sample mailboxes, triage results and a canned AI provider, then saves PNGs to screenshots/. It needs no mail account or Ollama, and also asserts a few UI behaviours such as the email context menu.

nodes.name: CannedAi
nodes.summary: Fake AiProvider returning fixed model lists and scripted outputs (quick-reply JSON or a markdown summary) so AI features render deterministically in screenshots.

nodes.name: mail
nodes.summary: Builds a sample MimeMessage with sender, subject, body, relative date and seen/flagged flags, assigning descending UIDs.

nodes.name: loadFonts
nodes.summary: Loads Roboto and Material Icons from the Flutter SDK cache so test renders show real text and icons instead of placeholder boxes.

nodes.name: snap
nodes.summary: Pumps the widget tree, captures the RepaintBoundary as a 1.5x PNG and writes it to the screenshots directory.

nodes.name: sampleState
nodes.summary: Creates an AppState backed by mocked SharedPreferences and loads three demo accounts (Gmail, Microsoft university, side project) with mailboxes, messages, triage and a CannedAi-backed EmailAi via debugLoad.

nodes.name: app
nodes.summary: Wraps AppState in a Provider and RepaintBoundary, rendering either the full HearthmailApp or a single page with the app's theme.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Defines widget tests that produce each screenshot: home with summary and quick replies, right-click menu (also checks VIP adding), dark priority view, composer, first-run and Microsoft setup, university reply and phone layout.

nodes.name: user_data.dart
nodes.summary: Defines the user's on-device personal mail organization: VIPs, blocked senders, muted threads, snoozes/reminders, follow-ups, scheduled ('send later') mail, templates, per-account signatures and an autocomplete contact book, all persisted as one JSON blob in SharedPreferences. Keeping this state local (rather than on the IMAP server) is a deliberate privacy choice and lets features like snooze and send-later work with any provider.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Dart 3 records (e.g. `(String, int)` for contacts and `(String email, String name)` for suggestions) and factory `fromJson` constructors for lightweight serialization without codegen.

nodes.name: Snooze
nodes.summary: Immutable record of a message the user asked to be reminded about; it is hidden from the inbox until `until`. Stores the mailbox path and UID too so the message can be brought back even if it is no longer loaded in memory.

nodes.name: FollowUp
nodes.summary: Immutable record of a sent message the user wants to be nudged about if nobody replies by `due`; drives the 'Follow up' view and the follow-up compose flow.

nodes.name: ScheduledMail
nodes.summary: Serializable snapshot of an outgoing message queued for 'Send later', including recipients, body, threading headers and attachment file paths, so it can be delivered later by the app's timer even after a restart.

nodes.name: Template
nodes.summary: A named reusable message body the user can insert from the composer's Templates dialog.

nodes.name: UserData
nodes.summary: Central container for all locally kept user mail-organization data with load/save to SharedPreferences, VIP and block checks, and a frequency-weighted contact book for recipient autocomplete. An in-memory constructor exists for tests and previews.

nodes.name: open
nodes.summary: Async factory that loads the persisted `userdata.v1` JSON from SharedPreferences into a new UserData, silently ignoring corrupt data so a bad blob never blocks app start.

nodes.name: _load
nodes.summary: Populates every collection (VIPs, blocked, muted, snoozes, follow-ups, scheduled mail, templates, signatures, contacts) from a decoded JSON map, tolerating missing keys.

nodes.name: save
nodes.summary: Persists the whole UserData blob to SharedPreferences, first pruning the contact book to the 3000 most-used addresses to keep storage bounded.

nodes.name: noteContact
nodes.summary: Records (or reinforces with a weight) an email address and display name for autocomplete, skipping no-reply addresses; returns whether anything changed so callers know to save.

nodes.name: suggestContacts
nodes.summary: Returns the best autocomplete matches for a typed prefix, matching email start or any word of the display name, ranked by how often the contact has been seen.

nodes.name: compose_page.dart
nodes.summary: Full-screen message composer used for new mail, replies, reply-all, forwards, follow-up nudges and restoring an undone send. Besides recipient autocomplete, templates, attachments, signatures, quoting, send-later and follow-up reminders, it hosts the AI writing tools (compose from notes, draft reply, rewrite styles, custom edits, translation, subject suggestion) which stream text straight into the body via local Ollama models.
nodes.languageNotes: A Flutter StatefulWidget whose State holds all TextEditingControllers; AI output arrives as a `Stream<String>` subscription that is cancelled on stop/dispose, and `PopScope` intercepts back navigation to offer saving a draft.

nodes.name: ComposePage
nodes.summary: Public StatefulWidget entry point for composing; its optional constructor parameters (replyTo, replyAll, forwardOf, aiReplyInstruction, initialBody, restore, followUpOf) select which compose mode the page opens in.

nodes.name: _ComposePageState
nodes.summary: State holding the composer's fields, attachments, AI stream subscription and undo buffer; implements prefill logic, validation, sending/scheduling, draft-on-leave, templates and the AI toolbar UI.

nodes.name: initState
nodes.summary: Prefills the composer depending on mode: restores an undone message, builds reply recipients/subject (excluding yourself for reply-all), sets 'Fwd:' and loads original attachments, or auto-drafts a follow-up nudge with AI; replies go out from the account that received the original. Also kicks off an AI reply draft when an instruction was passed and snapshots the initial state for dirty detection.

nodes.name: _loadForwardedAttachments
nodes.summary: Downloads the original message's attachments to files (via AppState.attachmentFiles) so a forward includes them, showing a loading chip meanwhile.

nodes.name: _runAi
nodes.summary: Generic driver for every AI writing action: saves the current body for undo, clears it, streams model chunks live into the body field, and on completion replaces it with a cleaned draft (EmailAi.cleanDraft); restores the old text on error.

nodes.name: _suggestSubject
nodes.summary: Asks the local model for a subject line based on the body text and fills the Subject field, with a spinner while waiting.

nodes.name: _finalBody
nodes.summary: Builds the text actually sent: appends the account's signature if missing, then either a forwarded-message block with the original headers and body or a '>'-quoted copy of the original for replies.

nodes.name: _validate
nodes.summary: Checks there is at least one recipient, that all To/Cc/Bcc addresses parse, and that a sending account exists, showing a snackbar for the first problem.

nodes.name: _mail
nodes.summary: Packs the composer state into an OutgoingMail (from account, recipients, subject, final body, reply target, files, optional send time and follow-up days) for AppState to send, schedule or save as draft.

nodes.name: _send
nodes.summary: Validates, confirms sending without a subject, refuses immediate send when the account is offline, then hands the OutgoingMail to AppState.sendMail (which supports undo-send and scheduling) and closes the page.

nodes.name: _sendLater
nodes.summary: Shows the 'Send later' dialog with preset times (tomorrow morning/afternoon, Monday) or a custom date via pickDateTime, then sends with that schedule.

nodes.name: _confirmLeave
nodes.summary: When the composer has unsaved changes, asks whether to discard, keep editing or save the message to the account's Drafts folder via AppState.saveDraft.

nodes.name: _templates
nodes.summary: Templates dialog: inserts a saved template into the body, deletes one, or saves the current body as a new named template, persisting changes through UserData.save.

nodes.name: _ComposePageState.build
nodes.summary: Builds the composer screen: back-navigation guard, Cmd+Enter/Escape shortcuts, app bar (attach, templates, markdown preview, follow-up reminder, split Send/Send-later button), from-account picker, recipient and subject fields, attachment chips, AI toolbar/writer, the body editor or rendered Markdown preview, and the quote/signature/follow-up footer.

nodes.name: _fromPicker
nodes.summary: Dropdown for choosing which connected account the message is sent from, rendering each with an AccountBadge and warning when the chosen account is offline.

nodes.name: _recipientField
nodes.summary: Address field with autocomplete: suggests previously seen contacts from UserData for the last comma-separated token and inserts a properly quoted 'Name <email>' entry.

nodes.name: _aiToolbar
nodes.summary: AI action strip above the body: while generating it shows progress and Stop; otherwise offers 'Write for me', rewrite styles (RewriteStyle), translate to the detected reply language or any common language, and Undo AI.

nodes.name: _aiWriter
nodes.summary: Prompt box for free-form AI writing: composes a new email from notes when the body is empty, or applies a custom edit instruction to existing text.

nodes.name: email_web_view.dart
nodes.summary: Renders an email's prepared HTML page in the platform web engine (WebKit/Chromium via webview_flutter) so messages look as their senders designed, opening any clicked link in the external browser. Falls back to a simpler built-in HTML widget where no web view exists (Windows, tests).

nodes.name: EmailWebView
nodes.summary: Public widget taking the HTML string and page background; its static `supported` getter decides whether a native web view can be used on the current platform.

nodes.name: _EmailWebViewState
nodes.summary: Owns the WebViewController, reloads only when the HTML actually changes, and chooses between the native web view and the HtmlWidget fallback.

nodes.name: _EmailWebViewState.initState
nodes.summary: Configures the web view: JavaScript only for the app's own fit-to-width script (the email's scripts are blocked by its CSP), a navigation delegate that blocks in-view navigation and launches clicked links externally, and the background color.

nodes.name: _EmailWebViewState.build
nodes.summary: Returns the native WebViewWidget when available, otherwise a scrollable HtmlWidget with readable text color derived from the background luminance and external link handling.

nodes.name: home_page.dart
nodes.summary: Top-level app shell: lays out sidebar, message list and reader as three panes on wide windows or one pane at a time (with a drawer) on phones, so one codebase serves desktop and mobile. Wires global Apple-Mail-style keyboard shortcuts, surfaces AppState toasts as snackbars, reopens undone sends in the composer, and offers the AI 'Catch me up' inbox digest.

nodes.name: HomePage
nodes.summary: Public StatefulWidget for the main window, shown by the app once accounts are configured.

nodes.name: _HomePageState
nodes.summary: State that subscribes to AppState toast and undone-send streams, owns the search focus node and phone navigation flag, and builds the responsive layout.

nodes.name: _HomePageState.initState
nodes.summary: Subscribes to AppState.toasts (shown as SnackBars with optional actions) and AppState.undoneSends (re-opens the message in ComposePage for editing after 'Undo send' or a failed send).

nodes.name: _catchUp
nodes.summary: Opens the 'Catch me up' dialog: picks up to 30 unread inbox messages (or the latest 20 if fewer than 3 are unread) and streams an AI digest of them into an AiCard.

nodes.name: _HomePageState.build
nodes.summary: Builds the shell: registers shortcuts (new message, search, settings, reply/reply-all/forward, archive, delete, read/flag toggles, junk), app bar actions, and chooses the three-pane or single-pane phone layout based on window width (900px breakpoint).

nodes.name: message_list.dart
nodes.summary: The middle pane: search bar (keyword or AI semantic/natural-language search), view title and filter chips, and the scrollable list of message tiles for the current AppState view with infinite scrolling, right-click menus and phone swipe-to-archive/delete. Also renders the special Scheduled and Follow-up lists and an AI 'Answer' card that answers questions from search results.

nodes.name: formatListDate
nodes.summary: Formats a message date compactly for the list: time for today, weekday within the last 6 days, month-day this year, otherwise full date.

nodes.name: MessageListPane
nodes.summary: Public stateless pane that reads the current view from AppState and assembles the search bar, header with mark-all-read/refresh, list filters and the appropriate list body.

nodes.name: MessageListPane.build
nodes.summary: Computes the view title from the ViewKind, then lays out the search bar, header actions, search header or filter chips (All/Unread/Flagged/Attachments) and the list or the Scheduled/Follow-up special views.

nodes.name: _buildList
nodes.summary: Builds the message list body: loading/empty/connection-failed states with retry, then a separated ListView of MessageTiles with lazy loadMore near the bottom, right-click/long-press context menus, and on narrow screens Dismissible swipes (right archives, left deletes).

nodes.name: _SearchBarState
nodes.summary: Search field state with an AI toggle: submits either an AI (natural-language/semantic) or plain search to AppState, clears itself when the user leaves search, and shows a clear button.

nodes.name: _SearchHeaderState
nodes.summary: Shows search progress/status and, when the AI search completes for a question-like query (or the user clicks 'Ask AI'), an AiCard that streams an answer grounded in the top 6 results.

nodes.name: MessageTile
nodes.summary: Public row widget for one message: unread dot, VIP star, sender, flag/attachment icons, date, subject, two-line preview, and tags for reminders, suspicious mail, AI priority, needs-reply and category plus an optional account badge.

nodes.name: _ScheduledList
nodes.summary: Lists messages queued with 'Send later' from UserData, with Send now and Cancel actions.

nodes.name: _FollowUpList
nodes.summary: Lists follow-ups split into due (no reply yet, with a 'Follow up' button that opens ComposePage in follow-up mode) and waiting ones, each dismissible.

nodes.name: message_view.dart
nodes.summary: The reading pane and message actions: toolbar (reply, forward, archive, delete, flag, remind-me snooze, move, junk, VIP, mute, block), header with sender/recipients and safety banners (phishing, snooze, mailing list, blocked remote images), AI tools (summary, quick replies, AI-drafted reply, translation, add-to-calendar), attachments, and the sanitized email body via EmailWebView. Also exports shared helpers like openReply/openForward, snooze time choices and the right-click message menu.
nodes.languageNotes: Keyed by ObjectKey(message) so all per-message AI panel state resets when the selection changes; the parsed EmailDocument is memoized by a key of image/dark/translation flags to avoid re-parsing HTML on every rebuild.

nodes.name: openReply
nodes.summary: Pushes ComposePage as a reply (optionally reply-all), optionally with an AI instruction to auto-draft the reply or a preset body; shared by the toolbar, shortcuts, quick replies and context menu.

nodes.name: openForward
nodes.summary: Pushes ComposePage in forward mode for the given message.

nodes.name: snoozeChoices
nodes.summary: Returns the preset 'Remind me' times (in 1 hour, this evening, tomorrow morning, this weekend, next week), omitting ones that no longer make sense for the current time, like Apple Mail and Gmail.

nodes.name: pickDateTime
nodes.summary: Shows a date picker followed by a time picker and returns the combined DateTime, used for custom snooze and send-later times.

nodes.name: MessageView
nodes.summary: Public reading-pane widget: empty placeholder when nothing is selected, otherwise the toolbar plus a per-message body (spinner while the full message loads).

nodes.name: MessageToolbar
nodes.summary: Public action bar for the selected message with reply/forward, archive, delete, flag, snooze menu, and a More menu (move, junk, read/unread, VIP, mute, block with confirmation); adapts to narrow screens.

nodes.name: _MessageBodyState
nodes.summary: Per-message state for the reader: language detection and streamed translation, AI summary and quick-reply panels, calendar event extraction, unsubscribe, remote-image opt-in, and a cached EmailDocument built from HTML or plain text.

nodes.name: _translate
nodes.summary: Streams an AI translation of subject and body into the user's language, showing it in place of the original (re-showing a cached translation if available) and toasting on failure.

nodes.name: _addToCalendar
nodes.summary: Uses the AI to extract an event (title, time, location) from the email, shows it for confirmation, then asks AppState to open it in the system calendar.

nodes.name: _unsubscribe
nodes.summary: Confirms and then performs a mailing-list unsubscribe through AppState.unsubscribe, reporting the result as a toast.

nodes.name: _document
nodes.summary: Builds (and memoizes) the EmailDocument shown in the web view: the translation as plain text, the sanitized HTML with remote images allowed only on opt-in and cid: inline images embedded as data URIs, or the plain-text body.

nodes.name: _MessageBodyState.build
nodes.summary: Lays out the reader: subject, sender with VIP toggle, recipients, date and account badge, warning/info banners (suspicious, snoozed, language/translation, mailing list, blocked images), AI bar and cards, attachment chips, and the body in an EmailWebView (white page for HTML even in dark mode).

nodes.name: _aiBar
nodes.summary: Row of AI actions for the open email: Summarize, Quick replies, Add to Calendar, Translate, and an inline 'Reply with AI' instruction field that opens the composer with an AI-drafted reply.

nodes.name: _quickReplyCard
nodes.summary: AiCard listing the AI's short suggested replies; clicking one opens the composer that expands it into a full editable reply.

nodes.name: _AttachmentChipState
nodes.summary: Chip for one attachment that opens it (click) or saves it to Downloads (download icon) via AppState.saveAttachment, with busy spinner and human-readable size.

nodes.name: showMessageMenu
nodes.summary: Apple-Mail-like right-click/long-press context menu for a message offering reply, forward, read/flag, remind me, archive, move, junk, delete, VIP, mute, copy sender and block, dispatching each to AppState.

nodes.name: sidebar.dart
nodes.summary: Left navigation pane listing All Inboxes, VIPs, Reminders, Scheduled and Follow-up views, the AI 'Smart inbox' (Priority, Needs reply and per-category views with a re-sort button), and each account's folders with connection status. Also provides shared color/icon helpers and the AccountBadge widget used elsewhere.

nodes.name: categoryColor
nodes.summary: Maps each AI triage MailCategory to a fixed color so category tags and sidebar dots are consistent across the app.

nodes.name: accountColor
nodes.summary: Returns a distinct color per account index (cycling through 8) for account dots and badges.

nodes.name: mailboxIcon
nodes.summary: Chooses an icon for an IMAP mailbox from its role flags (inbox, sent, drafts, trash, junk, archive, all, flagged), defaulting to a folder.

nodes.name: Sidebar
nodes.summary: Public sidebar widget; `onNavigate` lets the phone drawer close after a selection.

nodes.name: _SidebarState
nodes.summary: Builds the navigation list from AppState: unified/VIP/reminder/scheduled/follow-up items with unread counts, the AI smart-inbox section (only when AI is ready), expandable per-account folder lists with connection retry, an 'Add account' button and an AI-offline warning with retry.

nodes.name: AccountBadge
nodes.summary: Public small colored dot plus email label identifying which account a message belongs to; reused in the message list, reader and composer's from-picker.

nodes.name: ai_widgets.dart
nodes.summary: Reusable widgets for presenting AI output: a minimal Markdown renderer for model text, a view that streams an AI response token-by-token with a copy button, and a tinted card that visibly marks content as AI-generated.

nodes.name: MarkdownText
nodes.summary: Renders the small Markdown subset local models emit (bold, bullets/numbered lists, headings, paragraphs) as selectable rich text, avoiding a full Markdown dependency in the reader.

nodes.name: inline
nodes.summary: Splits a line into TextSpans, making **bold** segments semibold.

nodes.name: AiStreamView
nodes.summary: Public widget that takes a stream factory and shows the AI text as it arrives, with an optional completion callback and placeholder.

nodes.name: _AiStreamViewState
nodes.summary: Subscribes to the AI stream once on init, buffers chunks, shows a spinner until the first token, renders progress via MarkdownText, offers Copy when done, shows errors inline, and cancels the subscription on dispose.

nodes.name: AiCard
nodes.summary: Public tinted container with a sparkle icon and title marking AI-generated content, with optional trailing widget and close button.

nodes.name: search_plan.dart
nodes.summary: Defines SearchPlan, the structured query the local AI produces from a natural-language search question (e.g. 'invoices from Acme last month'), and translates it into either standard IMAP SEARCH criteria or Gmail X-GM-RAW query syntax. Keeping the AI output as a plain value object decouples the language model from the mail protocol, so the same plan can drive any IMAP server.
nodes.languageNotes: Immutable Dart value class with a const constructor, nullable fields and a lenient factory constructor; uses collection-if/for inside list literals.

nodes.name: SearchPlan
nodes.summary: Immutable value object holding the filters of a mail search: keywords, from/to/subject, since/before dates and unread/flagged/attachment toggles. It is the contract between the AI planner (EmailAi.planSearch) and MailService.search, and offers converters to IMAP and Gmail syntax plus a human-readable description.

nodes.name: SearchPlan.fromJson
nodes.summary: Factory that leniently parses the JSON a local LLM returns: blank strings and the literal 'null' become null, unparseable dates are dropped, empty keywords are filtered and booleans must be exactly true. This tolerance exists because small local models often emit sloppy JSON.

nodes.name: withoutKeywords
nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the plan with keywords (and subject) removed, keeping sender, date and flag filters. Used as a fallback when a keyword search is too narrow, e.g. to combine structured filters with semantic ranking.

nodes.name: isEmpty
nodes.summary: Getter that is true when the plan sets no filter at all. MailService.search uses it to avoid sending an empty X-GM-RAW query to Gmail and fall back to IMAP 'ALL'.

nodes.name: describe
nodes.summary: Builds a short human-readable sentence such as 'about "invoice", from acme, after 2026-10-01' shown above search results, so the user can see how the AI interpreted their question; returns 'recent mail' for an empty plan.

nodes.name: toImapCriteria
nodes.summary: Converts the plan into RFC 3501 IMAP SEARCH criteria that work on any server: FROM/TO/SUBJECT with quoted, escaped values, SINCE/BEFORE dates in IMAP's d-Mon-yyyy format, UNSEEN/FLAGGED, and keywords chained with nested binary OR TEXT terms. Returns 'ALL' when nothing is set. Note that hasAttachment has no portable IMAP equivalent and is silently ignored here.

nodes.name: toGmailQuery
nodes.summary: Converts the plan into Gmail's web search syntax (from:, after:yyyy/mm/dd, is:unread, is:starred, has:attachment, OR-ed keywords) for use with the X-GM-RAW IMAP extension, which gives Gmail accounts the same smarter search as the Gmail UI.

nodes.name: html_text.dart
nodes.summary: Small HTML utilities for email bodies: converts HTML mail into readable plain text (for AI prompts, previews and search indexing) and strips remote images to block tracking pixels. Both parse with package:html rather than regexes, for robustness against messy marketing HTML.

nodes.name: htmlToText
nodes.summary: Parses HTML, drops script/style/head/title/noscript, then walks the DOM collapsing whitespace, inserting line breaks after block elements, '- ' bullets for list items and appending link URLs that differ from their visible text. The result is compact, structured plain text that keeps meaning for the local AI without wasting context on markup.

nodes.name: blockRemoteImages
nodes.summary: Removes elements whose src is an http(s) URL (typical tracking pixels) while keeping inline cid: images, returning the original string untouched when nothing was removed. This is the privacy default unless the user chooses to load remote content.

nodes.name: mail_service.dart
nodes.summary: The protocol layer for one mail account: wraps enough_mail's MailClient to list folders, page and search messages (with Gmail X-GM-RAW support), flag, move, archive, junk, delete, download attachments, build Markdown-to-HTML messages and send them via SMTP. Every network operation is serialized through a per-account queue because IMAP state (the selected folder) is shared, and a static helper section extracts display and AI-ready data (subject, sender, body text, thread keys, unsubscribe links, phishing hints) from MimeMessage.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a Dart 3 sealed class with exhaustive switch pattern matching (PasswordCredentials(:final password)), a Future-chain mutex (_tail) for serialization, Expando as a weak per-object cache, and the null-aware list element syntax [?references, ...].

nodes.name: MailCredentials
nodes.summary: Sealed base type for how an account authenticates, so MailService can switch exhaustively between password and OAuth login.

nodes.name: PasswordCredentials
nodes.summary: Credentials variant carrying a plain IMAP/SMTP password (or app password) for classic logins.

nodes.name: OAuthCredentials
nodes.summary: Credentials variant carrying an OAuth token, the OAuthClient able to refresh it, and an optional onTokenRefreshed callback so refreshed tokens can be persisted (e.g. to the keychain) instead of forcing a new sign-in.

nodes.name: MailService
nodes.summary: Owns one account's MailClient and exposes every mail operation the app needs. Its constructor builds the MailAccount, sets a 256 KB 'download whole message' limit so previews and AI triage need no extra round trips, sets 30s/10s timeouts and wires OAuth token refresh and persistence. All server operations go through _serial so a background refresh can never interleave with a folder-specific action (avoiding e.g. deleting message 12 in the wrong folder).

nodes.name: Unsubscribe
nodes.summary: Value object describing how to leave a mailing list: an optional web URL, an optional mailto URL, and whether the web URL supports RFC 8058 one-click POST unsubscribe.

nodes.name: _account
nodes.summary: Static factory that maps an AccountConfig plus credentials to an enough_mail MailAccount, choosing STARTTLS vs implicit SSL per protocol and using an exhaustive switch over the sealed credential types (password login vs OAuth/XOAUTH2).

nodes.name: _serial
nodes.summary: Per-account async mutex: chains each operation onto the _tail future so IMAP commands run strictly one at a time, and swallows errors on the tail so one failure does not block the queue. If an operation fails with something that looks like a dropped connection it reconnects once and re-runs the operation. Risk: the retry is blind to idempotency, so it also re-runs SMTP sends (sendBuilt/saveDraft) and moves; if the first attempt actually reached the server before the error, the message can be sent or moved twice.

nodes.name: _looksLikeConnectionLoss
nodes.summary: Heuristic that treats a SocketException or any error whose text mentions 'connection', 'socket', 'not connected', 'broken pipe' or 'closed' as a lost connection. It is deliberately broad to recover from sleep/Wi-Fi changes, but substring matching can also misclassify unrelated errors and trigger a retry.

nodes.name: _reconnect
nodes.summary: Best-effort disconnect followed by a fresh connect (30s timeout), used by _serial before retrying an operation after a connection drop.

nodes.name: _ensure
nodes.summary: Selects the given mailbox only if it is not already the selected one, avoiding redundant SELECT round trips; every folder-specific operation calls it first because IMAP commands act on the currently selected folder.

nodes.name: mailboxes
nodes.summary: Lists the account's folders ordered Inbox, Flagged, Drafts, Sent, Archive, All Mail, Junk, Trash and then the rest, filtering out non-selectable container folders, to populate the sidebar.

nodes.name: fetchPage
nodes.summary: Fetches one page (default 40) of newest-first messages from a folder. It always re-SELECTs so the message count is current, returns empty for empty folders or out-of-range pages, fetches whole bodies for messages under the size limit, and sorts by date descending.

nodes.name: ensureFull
nodes.summary: Returns the message unchanged if a body is already present, otherwise downloads its full contents (60s timeout) in the right folder; used when opening a message that was only partially fetched.

nodes.name: hasBody
nodes.summary: Static check whether a MimeMessage already contains a decodable text/plain or text/html part.

nodes.name: searchFolder
nodes.summary: Chooses which folder to search for 'all my mail': Gmail's All Mail when the account is Gmail, otherwise the Inbox, otherwise the first folder.

nodes.name: search
nodes.summary: Runs a server-side search for a SearchPlan. On Gmail with a non-empty plan it sends a UID SEARCH using X-GM-RAW with the plan's Gmail query (backslashes removed and quotes escaped so it fits in one IMAP quoted string), so results match Gmail's own search engine; elsewhere it uses standard IMAP criteria. It then fetches only the newest `limit` UIDs and sorts them newest first.

nodes.name: setSeen
nodes.summary: Marks a message read or unread on the server (in its folder) and mirrors the flag on the local MimeMessage so the UI updates immediately.

nodes.name: setFlagged
nodes.summary: Stars or unstars a message on the server and mirrors the change on the local object.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Deletes a message from its folder via enough_mail (which moves to Trash or expunges depending on server).

nodes.name: archive
nodes.summary: Moves a message to the Archive folder, or to All Mail when there is none, which on Gmail is equivalent to Gmail's own Archive (removes the Inbox label). Throws a user-facing MailException when no archive target exists or the message is already there.

nodes.name: fetchByUids
nodes.summary: Fetches specific messages by UID from a folder, sorted newest first; used to open hits returned by the local semantic search index.

nodes.name: moveTo
nodes.summary: Moves a message to another folder, doing nothing if source and target are the same.

nodes.name: junk
nodes.summary: Moves a message to the Junk/Spam folder (on Gmail this also trains the spam filter), throwing if the account has no Junk folder.

nodes.name: moveToInbox
nodes.summary: Moves a message back to the Inbox, e.g. when a snooze ends or a message is un-archived; silently no-ops when there is no Inbox or it is already there.

nodes.name: fetchPart
nodes.summary: Returns an attachment part, using the locally cached bytes when the message was fetched whole and otherwise downloading just that MIME part (2 minute timeout for large files).

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds an outgoing MimeMessage from a Markdown body: renders GitHub-flavoured Markdown to styled HTML plus a plain-text alternative, uses multipart/mixed when there are file attachments or forwarded parts, sets recipients and subject, and sets reply threading either from the original message or from raw In-Reply-To/References headers (for replies to messages no longer loaded). Separating build from send lets the compose flow save drafts or queue/undo sends with the same message.

nodes.name: sendBuilt
nodes.summary: Sends a pre-built message through SMTP (enough_mail also appends a copy to Sent), then best-effort marks the original as Answered. Because the send runs inside _serial, a connection-like error after the server already accepted the message triggers a reconnect and second send, risking a duplicate email.

nodes.name: saveDraft
nodes.summary: Saves an unfinished message to the account's Drafts folder through the serialized queue (also subject to _serial's retry, so a duplicate draft is possible after a flaky connection).

nodes.name: send
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that builds a message with build() and immediately sends it with sendBuilt().

nodes.name: fetchRange
nodes.summary: Fetches messages counted back from the newest after skipping `skip`, optionally headers-only; used by the background semantic search indexer (on its own connection) to walk a folder page by page.

nodes.name: subjectOf
nodes.summary: Returns a message's decoded subject (falling back to the envelope) trimmed, or '(no subject)'.

nodes.name: senderOf
nodes.summary: Returns the first From address of a message (header or envelope) or null.

nodes.name: senderName
nodes.summary: Returns the sender's display name, falling back to the email address or 'Unknown sender', for list rows.

nodes.name: displayList
nodes.summary: Formats a list of addresses with friendly names only (e.g. 'Alex Rivera, bob@y.com') for display.

nodes.name: addressList
nodes.summary: Formats addresses in full RFC form ('Name <a@b>') so they can be edited and re-parsed with parseAddresses.

nodes.name: bodyText
nodes.summary: Returns the best plain-text body: the text/plain part if non-empty, otherwise HTML converted with htmlToText. The result is cached per message in an Expando (a weak map) because HTML conversion is too slow to redo on every list repaint.

nodes.name: keyOf
nodes.summary: Produces a stable cache key for a message (its Message-ID, or 'folder#uid' as a fallback) so AI results such as summaries and triage labels can be cached and reused.

nodes.name: toContent
nodes.summary: Converts a MimeMessage into the protocol-independent EmailContent model (id, from, to, subject, date, plain body, unread) that the AI layer consumes, keeping enough_mail types out of the AI code.

nodes.name: unsubscribeOf
