nodes.summary: Parses List-Unsubscribe (RFC 2369) for the first http(s) and mailto targets and checks List-Unsubscribe-Post (RFC 8058) for one-click support, which is only trusted over https. Returns an Unsubscribe or null when the email offers no way out.

nodes.name: suspicionOf
nodes.summary: Simple phishing heuristic: flags a sender whose display name contains a different email domain than the real From address, or names a well-known brand (PayPal, Apple, Microsoft, DHL...) that the sending domain does not contain. Returns a plain-English warning or null; it is a hint, not authentication (no SPF/DKIM checks), and can false-positive on legitimate third-party senders.

nodes.name: threadKeyOf
nodes.summary: Computes a conversation key shared by all messages in a thread: the first (root) Message-ID in References, else In-Reply-To, else the message's own Message-ID, else the normalized subject. Used to group messages into conversations without server-side threading support.

nodes.name: normalizedSubject
nodes.summary: Strips any chain of reply/forward prefixes in several languages (Re, Fwd, AW, WG, SV, VS, TR, RIF, with optional [n] counters) and lowercases the subject for subject-based thread grouping.

nodes.name: markdownToPlain
nodes.summary: Converts light Markdown to tidy plain text for the text/plain part: removes bold markers and heading hashes and rewrites links as 'text (url)'.

nodes.name: parseAddresses
nodes.summary: Splits a comma/semicolon separated recipient string like 'Ann <ann@x.com>, bob@y.com' and parses each entry into a MailAddress, throwing on malformed input so the compose UI can report it.

nodes.name: widget_test.dart
nodes.summary: Unit tests (despite the Flutter template name) for pure logic: SearchPlan IMAP/Gmail query generation, quote escaping and lenient JSON parsing; htmlToText and blockRemoteImages; EmailAi.cleanDraft output cleanup; and MailService.parseAddresses and markdownToPlain. They need no network, mail server or Ollama.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Test entry point defining the SearchPlan group and standalone tests that pin exact IMAP criteria and Gmail query strings, address parsing and text-cleanup behaviour, guarding the parts most likely to regress silently.

nodes.name: FEATURES.md
nodes.summary: Feature-by-feature comparison of Hearthmail against Apple Mail and Gmail (built, planned, limited, impossible) across reading, writing and search, plus benchmarked local-model assignments (gemma4, embeddinggemma, translategemma) and an explanation of how the local semantic vector search works.

nodes.name: OAUTH_SETUP.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step guide for registering your own Google Cloud and Microsoft Entra OAuth apps (Gmail API, IMAP.AccessAsUser.All/SMTP.Send, http://localhost redirect, public client flows) so Hearthmail can offer "Sign in with Google / Microsoft", with troubleshooting and privacy notes on Keychain token storage.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project overview of Hearthmail: the local-Ollama AI features and where they live in the UI, required models, how to run/build on macOS, multi-account sign-in options, the lib/ project layout, other-platform notes and test commands.

nodes.name: analysis_options.yaml
nodes.summary: Dart analyzer configuration that enables the flutter_lints recommended rule set and excludes build output and native platform folders (android, ios, macos, windows) from analysis.

nodes.name: pubspec.yaml
nodes.summary: Flutter package manifest for hearthmail (Dart SDK ^3.14) declaring runtime dependencies such as enough_mail (IMAP/SMTP), http (Ollama/OAuth), flutter_secure_storage (Keychain), webview_flutter, provider, file_selector, path_provider and markdown, plus flutter_lints for development.
nodes.languageNotes: Most of the file is the stock flutter create commentary; the meaningful content is the dependencies block and uses-material-design.

nodes.name: AndroidManifest.xml
nodes.summary: Android app manifest for the Flutter host activity: grants INTERNET permission and enables cleartext HTTP traffic (needed to reach a LAN Ollama server over plain http), sets the "Hearthmail" label and declares the PROCESS_TEXT query used by the Flutter engine.

nodes.name: Info.plist
nodes.summary: iOS bundle Info.plist for the Runner app: display name "Hearthmail", Flutter build name/number versioning, scene-based lifecycle via SceneDelegate, launch storyboard and supported orientations for iPhone and iPad.

nodes.name: AppInfo.xcconfig
nodes.summary: Xcode build settings for the macOS Runner target defining the product name "Hearthmail", bundle identifier app.hearthmail.hearthmail and copyright, and optionally including a local Signing.xcconfig.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the optional include directive `#include? "Signing.xcconfig"` so builds work whether or not the developer has created a signing file.

nodes.name: Signing.xcconfig.example
nodes.summary: Template for a developer-local Signing.xcconfig setting DEVELOPMENT_TEAM and the Apple Development code-sign identity, so local builds keep a stable signature and macOS does not re-prompt for Keychain access after every rebuild.

nodes.name: DebugProfile.entitlements
nodes.summary: Debug/Profile build macOS sandbox entitlements: app-sandbox confines the app; network.client allows outbound IMAP/SMTP, OAuth token and Ollama connections; network.server allows the loopback HTTP server that receives the OAuth redirect; files.user-selected.read-write lets the user attach chosen files; files.downloads.read-write lets attachments be saved to Downloads. Also enables cs.allow-jit for the Dart VM during development.

nodes.name: Release.entitlements
nodes.summary: Release build macOS sandbox entitlements: app-sandbox confines the app; network.client allows outbound IMAP/SMTP, OAuth token and Ollama connections; network.server allows the loopback HTTP server that receives the OAuth redirect; files.user-selected.read-write lets the user attach chosen files; files.downloads.read-write lets attachments be saved to Downloads. Matches the debug set minus allow-jit, since release builds are AOT-compiled.

nodes.name: Info.plist
nodes.summary: macOS bundle Info.plist for the Runner app, filling bundle name, identifier, copyright and minimum system version from xcconfig variables and Flutter build name/number.

nodes.name: model_bench.dart
nodes.summary: Standalone CLI benchmark that compares local Ollama models on the jobs Hearthmail gives them: embedding retrieval accuracy (top-1/top-3/MRR at several dimensions), reply-writing speed plus triage sorting accuracy, and translation quality, using a fixed synthetic email corpus.
nodes.languageNotes: Relies on Dart 3 records and destructuring patterns (e.g. `for (final MapEntry(key: model, value: (qf, df)) in ...)`) and switch statements without break.

nodes.name: benchEmbed
nodes.summary: Embeds the test corpus and queries with embeddinggemma and qwen3-embedding, then reports top-1/top-3 hit rates, MRR and latency at full, 512 and 256 truncated dimensions.

nodes.name: benchChat
nodes.summary: For each chat model, measures reply-writing throughput via Ollama eval counters and scores JSON-schema-constrained triage (category and priority) against labeled emails in batches of 10.

nodes.name: benchTranslate
nodes.summary: Translates sample emails in German, French, Hindi, Japanese and English with each model, using the translategemma-specific prompt format when applicable, and prints timing and output.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point dispatching to the embed, chat or translate benchmark based on the first argument, with default model lists.

nodes.name: sessionOf
nodes.summary: Returns the account session a loaded message belongs to, looked up in an Expando that tags every fetched MimeMessage with its owner account.

nodes.name: reconnect
nodes.summary: Reconnects one account (after an error or a sign-in fix) and, if auto-sort is on, re-runs AI sorting on its inbox.

nodes.name: snoozeOf
nodes.summary: Returns the Snooze ("Remind me") record for a message, keyed by Message-ID/folder, or null if it is not snoozed.

nodes.name: isVipMessage
nodes.summary: True when the sender is on the user's VIP list; VIP mail always counts as Priority and appears in the VIP view.

nodes.name: setFilter
nodes.summary: Sets the quick filter above the message list (all, unread, flagged, attachments) and notifies listeners.

nodes.name: setView
nodes.summary: Switches the message list to another view (All Inboxes, a folder, Priority, a category, search, …), clears the selection and leaves search mode when appropriate.

nodes.name: triageOf
nodes.summary: Returns the cached AI sorting result (category, priority, needs-reply, suspicious) for a message, or null if it has not been sorted yet.

nodes.name: contentOf
nodes.summary: Converts a MimeMessage into the plain EmailContent the AI layer works with (via MailService.toContent), using the folder the message was loaded from.

nodes.name: toggleRead
nodes.summary: Marks a message read/unread on the server through the shared _act helper (optimistic UI update, server call, rollback toast on failure).

nodes.name: toggleFlag
nodes.summary: Flags or unflags a message on the server through the shared _act helper.

nodes.name: deleteMessage
nodes.summary: Deletes a message on the server (moves to Trash) and removes it from the visible lists through _act.

nodes.name: archiveMessage
nodes.summary: Archives a message (Gmail: removes the Inbox label; others: moves to the Archive folder) and removes it from the visible lists through _act.

nodes.name: junkMessage
nodes.summary: Moves a message to Junk/Spam (on Gmail this also trains Gmail's spam filter) and removes it from the lists through _act.

nodes.name: moveMessage
nodes.summary: Moves a message to another folder of the same account and removes it from the current list through _act.

nodes.name: sendScheduledNow
nodes.summary: Sends a "Send later" message immediately instead of waiting for its scheduled time.

nodes.name: unsnooze
nodes.summary: Cancels a "Remind me" snooze so the message returns to the inbox right away, and persists the change.

nodes.name: toggleVip
nodes.summary: Adds or removes a sender address from the local VIP list and saves user data.

nodes.name: dismissFollowUp
nodes.summary: Removes a follow-up reminder ("nobody replied yet") without waiting for a reply.

nodes.name: clearSearch
nodes.summary: Leaves search mode: clears the query and results and returns to the view that was open before the search.

nodes.name: isBlocked
nodes.summary: True if an address is blocked, either exactly or by its "@domain"; blocked senders' mail is hidden and moved to Junk.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Hearthmail is a cross-platform Flutter email client for any IMAP/SMTP account whose AI assistant runs entirely on local Ollama models, so no email content leaves the computer. The README maps each AI feature (smart inbox, summaries, quick replies, AI search, Catch me up, translation) to where it lives in the UI and lists the models to pull, while FEATURES.md compares Hearthmail with Apple Mail and Gmail and explains which benchmarked local model does which job. Keep this feature map in mind: every later step implements one of these rows.
tour.languageLesson: Markdown tables are a compact way to document a feature matrix; FEATURES.md uses them to separate built, planned, limited and impossible features so the README can stay short and link to the detail.

tour.title: Entry Point and Packages
tour.description: main.dart opens the persisted SettingsStore, builds the single global AppState and mounts it with Provider, then defers account connection until after the first frame so the window appears instantly. The root MaterialApp routes first-time users to account setup and everyone else to the inbox. pubspec.yaml shows the building blocks you will meet next: enough_mail for IMAP/SMTP, http for Ollama and OAuth, flutter_secure_storage for the Keychain, webview_flutter and provider.
tour.languageLesson: WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback runs code after Flutter paints its first frame, a common trick to keep startup responsive while slow async work (network connects) begins in the background. pubspec.yaml uses caret constraints like ^3.14, meaning 'compatible versions from 3.14 up to, but not including, 4.0'.

tour.title: AppState: The Central Controller
tour.description: AppState is the most depended-upon file in the project: a single ChangeNotifier that owns every connected account, the current MailView, message actions, sending, snoozes, block/mute rules, AI setup, inbox sorting, semantic indexing and search. Screens bind to it and call its methods rather than talking to services directly, which is why it sits at the hub of the dependency graph. Expect each later step to show a service that AppState orchestrates.
tour.languageLesson: ChangeNotifier plus Provider is Flutter's simplest state-management pattern: the model calls notifyListeners() after mutating, and widgets that used context.watch<AppState>() rebuild automatically. Dart enums like ViewKind combined with const named constructors (MailView.scheduled()) give cheap, comparable value objects for UI state.

tour.title: Domain Models
tour.description: These plain value objects form the shared vocabulary between layers. AccountConfig holds connection settings and provider presets but deliberately excludes secrets from its JSON; EmailContent carries only the facts the AI needs, independent of enough_mail, so AI code is testable without a mail server; Triage models a sorting verdict (category, priority, needs reply, phishing) with JSON round-tripping for caching; SearchPlan is the structured query an AI produces, translatable into IMAP SEARCH or Gmail X-GM-RAW.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping model classes free of framework and library types (no Flutter, no enough_mail) is a decoupling technique: the AI layer depends only on these small classes, so it can be reused from command-line tools and unit tests.

tour.title: Pluggable Local AI Layer
tour.description: The AI stack is Flutter-independent and built in three tiers. AiProvider defines the abstraction (streaming chat, model listing, embeddings) so a different backend could be swapped in later; OllamaProvider implements it over HTTP against localhost:11434 with optional JSON-schema output; and EmailAi turns every assistant feature (summaries, digests, quick replies, drafting, rewriting, triage, search planning and ranking, Q&A, translation, calendar extraction) into prompts on top of any provider, consuming the EmailContent and Triage models from Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Dart extension methods let ai_provider.dart add helpers such as 'collect this Stream<String> into one string or decoded JSON' to existing types without subclassing. Streams (Stream<T>) are how token-by-token model output flows to the UI.

tour.title: Mail Transport: IMAP and SMTP
tour.description: MailService is the protocol layer for one account, wrapping enough_mail's MailClient to list folders, page and search messages (with Gmail X-GM-RAW support from SearchPlan), flag, move, archive, delete, download attachments and send Markdown-to-HTML mail over SMTP. Because IMAP keeps shared server-side state (the selected folder), every network operation goes through a per-account serial queue so concurrent calls from AppState cannot interleave. Its static helpers extract AI-ready data such as body text, thread keys, unsubscribe links and phishing hints.
tour.languageLesson: The _serial<T>(Future<T> Function() op) helper chains each operation onto the previous Future, a lightweight async mutex. Dart 3 'sealed class MailCredentials' with PasswordCredentials and OAuthCredentials subclasses lets switch statements be checked for exhaustiveness.

tour.title: Sign-In: OAuth and Keychain
tour.description: With no backend server, 'Sign in with Google / Microsoft' uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and a short-lived loopback HTTP server that catches the redirect, using the user's own client registration. AccountSetupPage offers Google, Microsoft or an app password with provider presets and autoconfig discovery, testing the connection before saving. SettingsStore then keeps settings and account lists in SharedPreferences but sends passwords and OAuth tokens to the OS keychain, and OAUTH_SETUP.md walks users through registering their own OAuth apps.
tour.languageLesson: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) has the app generate a random code_verifier and send only its SHA-256 hash (code_challenge) with the authorization request; the verifier is revealed when exchanging the code, so an intercepted code is useless. It is the standard OAuth flow for public clients that cannot keep a secret.

tour.title: Smart Inbox Triage
tour.description: The Smart inbox applies EmailAi triage from Step 5 to sort mail into Priority, Needs reply and categories like Work, Finance and Travel. TriageCache stores verdicts per account in a JSON file (capped at 5000 entries) so each email is classified by the model only once, and the Sidebar exposes All Inboxes, VIPs, Reminders and the per-category smart views with a re-sort button, all driven by AppState.

tour.title: Search: Keyword, AI and Semantic
tour.description: Search has three tiers that build on earlier steps. Keyword search goes straight to IMAP; AI search has EmailAi turn plain English into a SearchPlan that MailService runs as server filters, then ranks results by relevance; and semantic search uses VectorIndex, a tiny per-account vector database storing one normalized embedding per email and matching by exact cosine similarity. AppState fuses keyword and meaning-based matches with reciprocal rank fusion, and MessageList renders the search bar, results and an AI 'Answer' card for questions like 'when does my flight leave?'.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal rank fusion scores each result as the sum of 1/(k + rank) across the ranked lists it appears in, so items ranked well by both keyword and vector search rise to the top without needing their raw scores to be comparable. Cosine similarity on pre-normalized vectors reduces to a simple dot product.

tour.title: App Shell and Reading Pane
tour.description: HomePage lays out sidebar, message list and reader as three panes on wide windows or one at a time on phones, wires Apple-Mail-style keyboard shortcuts, and offers the AI 'Catch me up' digest. MessageView is the reading pane: a toolbar of actions, safety banners for phishing and blocked remote images, and AI tools for summary, quick replies, drafted reply, translation and add-to-calendar, rendered through the AiWidgets that stream model output token by token inside a card marked as AI-generated.
tour.languageLesson: Responsive Flutter layouts typically branch on LayoutBuilder or MediaQuery width: one widget tree produces a three-pane desktop layout or a single-pane phone layout with a Drawer, which is how one codebase serves macOS and mobile.

tour.title: Safe HTML Rendering
tour.description: Email HTML is untrusted, so EmailHtml turns raw bodies into safe, self-contained pages: it strips scripts and event handlers, enforces a nonce-based Content-Security-Policy, blocks remote images and tracking pixels unless allowed, embeds cid: inline images, scales wide newsletters and folds quoted history. EmailWebView then displays that page in the platform web engine via webview_flutter, opening clicked links in the external browser and falling back to a simpler HTML widget where no web view exists.
tour.languageLesson: A nonce-based Content-Security-Policy only allows scripts or styles carrying a random per-page nonce attribute, so any markup an attacker smuggles into an email cannot execute even if it survives sanitization: defence in depth.

tour.title: Composing and Sending
tour.description: ComposePage handles new mail, replies, forwards, follow-up nudges and restoring an undone send, with recipient autocomplete, templates, attachments, signatures and send-later options. Its AI writing tools (write from notes, draft reply, rewrite styles, custom edits, translation, subject suggestions) stream text from EmailAi into the body. On send, AppState holds an OutgoingMail for the undo-send delay, pushes cancelled sends back to the composer through a stream, and handles scheduled mail and follow-up reminders before MailService delivers over SMTP.
tour.languageLesson: AppState exposes undone sends as a StreamController<OutgoingMail>.broadcast(): broadcast streams allow multiple listeners, letting HomePage react to 'Undo' by reopening the composer without AppState knowing about any widget.

tour.title: Local Organization and Settings
tour.description: UserData keeps the user's personal mail organization on-device as one JSON blob: VIPs, blocked senders, muted threads, snoozes, follow-ups, scheduled mail, templates, signatures and a contact book. Storing this locally rather than on the IMAP server is a deliberate privacy choice that also lets snooze and send-later work with any provider. SettingsPage edits all of this plus the AI configuration (Ollama URL, fast, writing, embedding and translation models) and saves each change immediately through AppState.

tour.title: Platform Config and Entitlements
tour.description: The macOS app runs in the App Sandbox, and its entitlements map directly to features from earlier steps: network.client for IMAP/SMTP, OAuth and Ollama, network.server for the OAuth loopback redirect from Step 7, and user-selected and Downloads file access for attachments. The release set matches debug minus allow-jit, since release builds are AOT-compiled. AppInfo.xcconfig defines the bundle identity, Signing.xcconfig.example keeps a stable signature so macOS does not re-prompt for Keychain access, and the Android manifest allows cleartext HTTP to reach a LAN Ollama server.
tour.languageLesson: Entitlements are XML property lists of boolean keys such as com.apple.security.app-sandbox; each capability must be explicitly granted, so the file doubles as a reviewable list of everything the app may touch. xcconfig files are plain key = value build settings that can #include an optional local file for developer-specific signing.

tour.title: Tests and Model Benchmarks
tour.description: The tests target pure logic so they need no network, mail server or Ollama: features_test and widget_test cover HTML sanitization, SearchPlan query generation, the vector index, MailService header helpers, .ics export and UserData, while oauth_test fakes the browser against the real loopback server to verify PKCE and state checks. Developer tools complete the picture: ai_smoke exercises every EmailAi feature live, model_bench compares local models on retrieval, triage accuracy and translation, and screenshots_test renders real screens with a canned AI provider.
tour.languageLesson: Because AiProvider is an interface (Step 5), tests and screenshot tools can inject a fake provider that returns canned responses, which is the payoff of dependency inversion: deterministic tests without a running model.
